record.original_question: For every special case of the nonnegative-parameter planar rational system x_{n+1} = (a1 + b1 x_n + g1 y_n)/(A1 + B1 x_n + C1 y_n), y_{n+1} = (a2 + b2 x_n + g2 y_n)/(A2 + B2 x_n + C2 y_n), with nonnegative initial conditions and positive denominators, determine exactly which equilibria satisfy the equivalence between local asymptotic stability and global attractivity. In other words, characterize all special cases and equilibria for which local asymptotic stability implies global attractivity and global attractivity implies local asymptotic stability.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the planar rational system of difference equations
  x_{n+1} = (α₁ + β₁ xₙ + γ₁ yₙ)/(A₁ + B₁ xₙ + C₁ yₙ),
  y_{n+1} = (α₂ + β₂ xₙ + γ₂ yₙ)/(A₂ + B₂ xₙ + C₂ yₙ),  n = 0,1,2,…,
where all parameters α_i, β_i, γ_i, A_i, B_i, C_i (i=1,2) are nonnegative real numbers, the initial conditions (x₀,y₀) are nonnegative, and the denominators are positive for every n ≥ 0. By a "special case" of the system we mean a choice of which of the twelve parameters are zero and which are positive (so the special cases enumerate the possible reduced rational systems of this form). An equilibrium is a fixed point (x̄,ȳ) of the map defined by the right-hand side. Local asymptotic stability of an equilibrium is defined by the standard requirement that it be Lyapunov stable and that nearby orbits converge to it. Global attractivity of an equilibrium (with respect to the nonnegative invariant region on which the system is well defined) means that every admissible orbit converges to it.

Characterize, for every special case of the above system and every equilibrium of that special case, exactly when local asymptotic stability is equivalent to global attractivity. Specifically:
 (a) Determine all special cases and all equilibria for which local asymptotic stability implies global attractivity.
 (b) Determine all special cases and all equilibria for which global attractivity implies local asymptotic stability.
artifact.status_search_result: The full characterization across all special cases of the nonnegative planar rational system is an open problem repeatedly highlighted by Camouzis and Ladas. Although partial results exist (e.g., conditions under which local asymptotic stability implies global attractivity for certain monotone or competitive sub-cases, and many individual special cases analyzed in the literature), no complete classification of the equivalence between local asymptotic stability and global attractivity over all special cases and equilibria appears to have been established. Subsequent works tackle particular special cases but do not resolve the global question.

status_evidence.title: When does local asymptotic stability imply global attractivity in rational equations?
status_evidence.snippet: Camouzis and Ladas (2006) study sufficient conditions but treat only special families, leaving the general characterization open.
status_evidence.claim: The equivalence has only been addressed in specific cases, with the general classification remaining unresolved.

status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as an open problem in the original investigation of the planar rational system.

status_evidence.snippet: Monograph collecting open problems and conjectures on global stability of rational difference equations.
status_evidence.claim: The general equivalence question is repeatedly listed as an open problem/conjecture.
